title: 2nd Chance Rescue-Dog Shelter
description:
On August 9, 2019, Camp As Sayliyah service members visited 2nd Chance Rescue-Dog Shelter. Thirty-five service members brought donations and spent time with more than 90 dogs and 54 cats.

Interview:
Sgt. Lia Cater
A Company, 1st Battalion, 114th Infantry Regiment
Sgt. Jimmy Simmermon
B Company, 1st Battalion, 114th Infantry Regiment
keywords: Cats, Camp As Sayliyah, U.S. Army, rescue, shelter, dogs, animals

transcript.text: (patriotic music playing)
(animals heard in background)
- [Announcer] Soldiers and other service members
are building a legacy of outreach to local
animal shelters during their rotation in Qatar.
- [Woman 1] We are able to take service members
out and visit with these animals, provide help and
care to the rescues that we've come across
and just help to build morale for our soldiers
as well as helping out in the country.
You know being an assistant to the host nation
doing some good.
For myself it was a great morale booster.
It was the ability to go out and do something
good and spread good will and good cheer.
With the soldiers, taking them out has been a great
morale booster and just creature comforts that they
would normally have at home, which are
usually their animals.
- Depending on how many people go out there
and how many dogs you walk it is very tiring.
It is getting bigger, more people are hearing
about it and more people want to go.
A great thing for the soldier, it's a great thing
for the animals.
It's a great thing for both countries,
America and Qatar, to work on their
relationship with each other.
- [Woman 1] Now we've made such an impact that
Camp As Sayliyah knows about that and
if people would only give time
they would be surprised on what they receive back.
(patriotic music playing)
- [Announcer] This is Jane Art from Camp As Sayliyah, Qatar.
